clue.text: Around Christmas love to drink, resulting in unseemly behaviour

parts.note: around Christmas time is in December, abbreviated IN DEC
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
rum is a spirit, a strong drink

explanation.surface: Someone drinks too much over the festive season and behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, conduct that breaks the rules of good manners.

clue.text: Drive starts in Ipswich, motoring past Ely later

indicators.note: the starts of the following five words supply their opening letters in sequence

explanation.surface: A drive from Ipswich by car that goes past the cathedral city of Ely further on.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipswich and Ely are towns in East Anglia, in the east of England; 'Drive' looks like a road trip but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to push or urge them forward, a synonym of drive.

clue.text: Where rain goes? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: rain falls all the way to the earth beneath
an idiom meaning completely or perfectly, as in 'that suits me'

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely, and literally describes falling rain reaching the earth.

clue.text: Salad ingredient given to princess, one from Shakespeare

parts.note: cress is a peppery leaf used in salads
Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: A princess is served some salad greens, said to be by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'princess' tempts the solver to DI; here it is IDA, from Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is the faithless heroine of Shakespeare's play Troilus and Cressida, a character from his works.

clue.text: Solitary, confused opponent of Republicans

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the single word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: A lonely, muddled figure who stands against the republican cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports the monarchy, so opposes republicans who want it abolished.

clue.text: We bounce back up after moderate attack of disease

indicators.note: after places the turned word below the first piece in this down clue

parts.note: moderate means mild, not severe

indicators.note: in a down clue, bouncing back up reads the short word from bottom to top

explanation.surface: We recover after a mild bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a fungal growth that attacks plants, a form of plant disease.

clue.text: Form rank

definitions.meaning: a school form is a group of pupils of the same year
a rank or grade in a social or quality hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: A class is both a school form and a rank or category.

clue.text: Powerful businessman?

parts.note: read as a company man, an abbreviation for company followed by a word for a gentleman; the whole means convincing

explanation.definitionFit: Cogent means powerful and persuasive, as of a strong argument.

clue.text: Actually, answer has been concealed by a small number away from work

indicators.note: something concealed by another is held within it, so the abbreviation goes inside the phrase

parts.note: a smatter is a small amount, a smattering
off means away, as in off work
an act is a piece of work or deed

explanation.surface: An answer was hidden by a few people who were absent from their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in fact or in reality, just like actually.

clue.text: Provide diversion — kids react badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Children respond poorly when someone tries to distract them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to divert attention from the main issue.

clue.text: Ground — one captured by the German military, finally

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war, someone captured
der is a German word for the

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A prisoner held by the German army, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground into fine particles means powdery, the past participle as adjective.

clue.text: Haul girl around, she's a slowcoach

indicators.note: around turns the two pieces back to front as one run

parts.note: to haul is to drag
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a girl about, complaining that she is too slow.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who falls behind, a straggler or slowcoach.

clue.text: Flower in parcel to America

parts.note: a lot is a parcel of goods at auction
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A bloom sent in a package to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant whose blossom is a famous flower in Asian art.

clue.text: After prolonged spell in bed, hesitate to prepare a trap

indicators.note: After places the hesitating word behind the time in bed

parts.note: a lie-in is a long stay in bed in the morning
to wait is to hold back or hesitate

explanation.surface: After a long sleep-in someone dithers.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush, setting a trap for a victim.

clue.text: How to produce a hyphen and make a stylish impression

definitions.meaning: literally, slicing a short line to make a hyphen
an idiom for looking dashing and impressive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means appearing stylish, and literally means making a short horizontal line.

clue.text: Potholers have to become more humble

definitions.meaning: cave explorers must descend into underground passages
to back down from a position, conceding an argument

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to retreat from a stance, and literally to descend as cavers do.

clue.text: Tailless carnivore found in porch

indicators.note: without its tail, the creature loses its last letter

parts.note: a stoat is a small meat-eating mammal

explanation.surface: A predator without a tail is discovered sheltering in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greece, a kind of porch.

clue.text: Vulnerable to attack, with unpredictable outcome

definitions.meaning: of a contest, impossible to call

explanation.definitionFit: Wide open describes both an exposed position and a contest anyone could win.

clue.text: I am a little time behind schedule for sacrifice

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a mo is a moment, a short time
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for running slightly late.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as a sacrifice, especially by burning.

clue.text: Piece changed in time

indicators.note: changed letters are rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: A piece altered over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece or article among others.

clue.text: Chancellor puts stuff back into soup

indicators.note: into puts the turned word inside the soup

parts.note: bisk is a variant spelling of bisque, a rich soup

indicators.note: back reads the stuffing word in reverse

parts.note: to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: A government minister drops something back into a bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: BISK is a less common spelling of bisque; 'back' reverses the stuffing word before 'into' places it inside the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the first Chancellor of the German Empire.

clue.text: Character caught out Jewish sectarian

indicators.note: out means the abbreviation is removed from the longer word

parts.note: the essence of something is its intrinsic character
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A figure caught out is revealed as belonging to a Jewish sect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period.

clue.text: Unusual tactic employed by bookmakers

indicators.note: an unusual version is an altered arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Bookies resort to an odd trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the hand-signal code used by racecourse bookmakers in Britain to pass on betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The bookies' sign language is something used by bookmakers, so it is what they employ.

clue.text: Fools rent in the Windsor area

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Idiots rent property near Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is the English county containing Windsor and its royal castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor lies in the county of Berkshire, so the county is the area around it.

clue.text: Remove lid from box to reveal present

indicators.note: removing the lid of a word drops its first letter

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: Someone opens a box to reveal a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something is to present it, both as verbs.

clue.text: Castigated after a tedious selection

indicators.note: a selection is a run of letters taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone was told off after making a dull choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold, so rated means castigated.

clue.text: No let-up when rocking and rolling

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: A party that never lets up, rocking and rolling all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' looks like part of 'rocking and rolling' but is the definition, as in rolling in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in it means very rich, which is what opulent means.

clue.text: Agricultural labourer finds insect on vegetables

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the insect after the vegetables

parts.note: peas are vegetables
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A farmworker discovers a bug on the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor farm worker who works the land.

clue.text: Elbow and back, say, getting brown

indicators.note: back reads both pieces together in reverse as one run

parts.note: say signals an example, abbreviated e.g.
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone's elbow and back turning brown.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to nudge them with the arm.

clue.text: Swollen-headed, called round on one occasion

indicators.note: round puts the first word around the other

parts.note: cited means called, as in summoned to court
once means on a single occasion

explanation.surface: Someone vain dropped by once.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain and arrogant, having a swollen head.
